title: Surgical failover and customer comms for mixed-deployment model regressions
creator: Ava Chen
description: Provide a low-risk, tenant-aware 'surgical failover' procedure and standardized customer communication templates to rapidly remediate model rollout regressions that surface differently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Scope covers detection -> targeted traffic diversion -> KV-cache reconciliation -> graceful pinning -> external comms and follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook that can be executed by oncall in <30 minutes for hosted and dedicated
Playbook includes steps for private deployments with customer liaison checklist
Standardized external comms templates and approved legal wording
Automated dashboard links and a single-command traffic diversion (where available) documented
Post-incident tasks and ownership for KV-cache reconciliation and model pinning
comments: 2026-02-10 Samira Patel: Triage call notes — multiple tenants reported hallucination spike on model v2026-02-09-rc2. Initial suspicion: subtle tokenization change in optimized kernel during quantized path. Impacted: hosted and dedicated; one private customer reported via SE.

2026-02-11 Marcus Lee: Proof-of-concept 'surgical' traffic diversion implemented in staging. Uses tenant slice routing to pin to prior model variant and disable quantized kernel for that slice. Preliminary latency impact <5ms.
2026-02-12 QA: Added end-to-end test that simulates KV-cache mismatch on rollback. Found edge-case where cached prefixes persisted across slice pinning — added explicit KV cache flush step.
2026-02-13 Legal (Nina Ramos): Reviewed external comms template; requested removal of predictive language and inclusion of customer remediation steps. Updated template in Confluence.
2026-02-14 Oncall (Evan Morales): Ran the playbook during a simulated canary failure and recorded a 1.2x token cost increase during diversion; approved as acceptable for P0 incidents.

2026-02-15 Marcus Lee: Open PR with orchestration changes: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-orch/pull/427 (contains single-step diversion CLI and telemetry tags). Need code review from infra and runtime teams.
rollback_steps: Identify affected tenant slices from observability dashboard (dashboard link included in playbook)
Pin affected slice to last-good model version (use rollout-orch single-step CLI)
Flush KV cache for pinned slice and verify kv-cache counters reach zero
Verify model binary on serving nodes matches pinned variant; if mismatch, trigger live-patch to replace kernel
Monitor fidelity dashboards for 30 minutes; if regressions persist escalate to full rollback
Communicate to customers using approved template (link in playbook_links)
runbook_summary: Fast path: for hosted/dedicated use single-step slice pin + KV flush. Private path: coordinate with customer SE/infra; provide patch bundle and guided orchestration. Communications: use pre-approved templates and set next update cadence (15/60/240 minutes).
postmortem_actions: Schedule runtime regression test focused on quantized kernel and tokenization compatibility (owner: Research)
Add dashboard tile that correlates model binary hash with tokenization stats (owner: Observability)
Refine autoscaler to detect sudden per-slice latency increases and optionally hold rollouts (owner: Dedicated)
Create KB for SEs for private customers with step-by-step patch bundle instructions (owner: Solutions)
